neet_phy_u02_t02_2.working: Acceleration is zero only if velocity (magnitude and direction) is constant. Constant speed with changing direction still gives acceleration.

neet_phy_u02_t02_3.working: 54 km/h = 15 m/s; 2 min = 120 s; motion is along a straight line in one direction, so displacement = 15 × 120 = 1800 m.

neet_phy_u02_t02_4.working: A is true: the direction of velocity changes, so there is centripetal acceleration. R is true: constant velocity means constant magnitude. But R does not explain A.

neet_phy_u02_t02_5.working: I is correct, e.g. uniform circular motion. II: a change in velocity direction means velocity is not constant, so the motion is accelerated, i.e. non-uniform in the constant-velocity sense. This depends on the convention that uniform motion means constant velocity, so II is judged correct.
